blocks.content: The Vice-President, like the President, is elected not directly by the people but by the method of indirect election.

rows: Proportional representation via single transferable vote
Proportional representation via single transferable vote

items: Unlike the Presidential election, nominated members of Parliament participate in the election of the Vice-President.
Members of State Legislative Assemblies (MLAs) do NOT participate in the Vice-Presidential election.
Actions taken by the Vice-President before their election is declared void by the Supreme Court remain valid and effective.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Vice-President is elected indirectly by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament.
The electoral college includes both elected and nominated members of Parliament.
State Legislative Assemblies do not participate in the election of the Vice-President.
The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote via secret ballot.
All disputes regarding the Vice-Presidential election are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court of India, whose decision is final.
